python3 -c "
import json
import subprocess

entries = [
    {
        'prompt': 'I burned dinner again. I guess I\'m just hopeless in the kitchen.',
        'response': 'First of all, burning dinner doesn\'t make you hopeless — it makes you a person who\'s still trying, and that\'s something to respect. Every single good cook has a graveyard of scorched pans behind them. What actually matters is that you\'re practicing and caring enough to want to get better. Tonight, it\'s okay to order takeout or eat something simple and give yourself permission to be a work-in-progress. Tomorrow, you\'ve got another chance — maybe with the oven on low and a timer set. You\'re not failing; you\'re learning, and that takes time.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'Everyone at the office lunch seemed to have their own groups. I ate alone at my desk again.',
        'response': 'That\'s a lonely way to spend a lunch break, and it makes complete sense that it stings. Being around people but still feeling on the outside is its own special kind of ache — you\'re not imagining it. Wanting connection at work is totally normal, not weird or needy. The fact that you noticed this and reached out here tells me you haven\'t given up on being part of things, which matters. If you want, we could brainstorm a few low-pressure ways to start having small conversations next week — maybe asking one person about their weekend or volunteering for something that requires chatting. No rush though. And until then, eating at your desk doesn\'t mean you\'re alone in the world, even if it feels that way right now.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'I\'ve been trying to write a story for months and nothing I write is any good. Maybe I should just stop.',
        'response': 'Months of effort with no feeling of progress is genuinely draining, and it\'s completely understandable that you\'re doubting the whole thing. But let me say this: the gap between what you can see in your head and what comes out on the page is where every writer lives, not just struggling ones. You don\'t actually have to decide forever whether to stop or continue right now. What if, instead, you gave yourself permission to write something terrible for a week? No pressure, no judging, just letting your ideas exist in messy form. Sometimes the act of writing badly is exactly how we find our way back to writing that matters. Your voice is in there, even if it feels buried under disappointment for now.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'I want to learn to play guitar but I\'m 42 and feel like I\'ve missed my chance at new hobbies.',
        'response': 'Forty-two is not too late — it\'s just a number, even when it doesn\'t feel like one in the moment. I know there\'s this cultural narrative about youth being the only time for growth, but that\'s not true and your life proves it if you\'ve learned anything new at any point. Starting guitar at forty-two means you have patience, self-awareness, and reasons of your own for wanting to do this — not just because you felt like you should. Your fingers might be a little less forgiving than they were at twenty, but your dedication can make up for it ten times over. Buy a cheap guitar, find a beginner YouTube lesson, and give yourself one month of five minutes a day. See how it feels. You\'re not behind; you\'re right where you need to be to start.'
    },
    {
        'prompt': 'It\'s been three weeks since I moved to a new city for work and I miss my home so much it physically hurts.',
        'response': 'Three weeks is honestly still the rawest part, and that physical ache you\'re feeling? That\'s grief, and it\'s real and valid. You left behind a place that holds your routines, your history, your comfort — that\'s a genuine loss, not just a change of scenery. It\'s okay to not be over it yet and to feel homesick without shame. Some things that might help in the small way: make a cup of tea the way you back home, set your phone wallpaper to a place that feels like yours, or call someone who already knows your real story. You don\'t have to force yourself to love the new city right now. It\'s okay to just be somewhere new while your heart is still at the old place. Over time, they can coexist.'
    }
]

for entry in entries:
    json_str = json.dumps(entry)
    subprocess.run(['python3', 'scripts/add_entry.py'], input=json_str + '\n', text=True, check=True)
    print('Added entry:', entry['prompt'][:50] + '...')

print('All 5 entries added successfully!')
"
